title: Renewal uplift experiments + security questionnaire integration playbook
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
High-level goal: design and run controlled experiments that test (A) alternative true-up cadence and uplift rules at renewal and (B) multi-year prepay discounts, while operationalizing how security questionnaire completion status affects renewal uplift and contract offers. Deliver a playbook that Sales, Finance, Legal and Customer Success can use to execute experiments, evaluate uplift on ARR, and update T&Cs.

Background context: Sales teams report variability in renewal uplift capture when customers delay security questionnaire completion or contractual signatures. We currently default to a single uplift schedule and negotiate ad-hoc discounts for multi-year deals. This work combines a quantitative experiment framework with a mapping of security questionnaire and SOC/data flow completion states into renewal decision rules.
acceptance_criteria:
- Experiment specs for 3 cohorts (Control, Tiered-Uplift, Time-decay-Uplift) documented and approved by Finance and Legal.
- Analytical dashboard tracking uplift capture rate, realized ARR, churn, and customer satisfaction for each cohort.
- Playbook doc with step-by-step runbook: eligibility rules, messages, PR templates for Sales, and contract clause snippets for Legal.
- Security questionnaire gating logic integrated into renewal workflows (at minimum: flag added to renewal record, visible to AE/CS).
- Rollback criteria and legal sign-off documented.
- Pilot run completed across at least 40 accounts in Q2 with clear go/no-go recommendation.
notes: Experiment variants considered: flat percent true-up vs tiered percent by overage magnitude vs time-decay uplift that reduces over negotiation window.
Proposed uplift bands: 5% for <10% overage, 12% for 10-30%, 20% cap for >30%; consider absolute cap in dollars for high-spend customers.
Multi-year incentives: 6% off for 2-year, 12% off for 3-year when customers prepay at 90%+ committed spend usage in prior cycle.

Security questionnaire integration: define 3 statuses (not started, in-progress, completed). Only 'completed' unlocks highest discount tiers; 'in-progress' allowed conditional offers with short-term provisional terms.
Legal constraints: any default uplift must be surfaced as a line item on the renewal quote; changes to standard SOW or amortization of prepaid amounts require finance approval.
Data sources: billing events, contract database (DocuSign/CLM), security questionnaire tracker (Confluence form / Drive sheet), Console usage exports.
Risk: excessive uplift may accelerate churn in price-sensitive segments; gating by SQ could be perceived as friction in procurement for some enterprise buyers.

Pilot to start after dashboard instrumentation and Legal sign-off.
